title: Projection-evaluation word on ringed coefficient systems
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$, $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For every scheme $W$ use a small skeleton of $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, completed coefficient sheaf $R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$, and ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. On the vertical sequence site write $\mathcal Q_W(n,U)=(A_n)_W(U)$, $R_W^{\mathrm{const}}$ for the constant sequence ring, $\mathscr P$ for the one-point sequence topos, and $\mathcal A=(A_n)_n$ for its quotient ring [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Let $\rho_W:(W^{\mathrm{Tow}},\mathcal Q_W)\to(W^{\mathrm{Tow}},R_W^{\mathrm{const}})$ and $\rho_0:(\mathscr P,\mathcal A)\to(\mathscr P,R)$ be scalar restriction morphisms. Write $g_W^{\mathcal Q}$ and $g_W^R$ for point-sections morphisms to these one-point sequence topoi, with $g_W^R\rho_W=\rho_0g_W^{\mathcal Q}$. The symbol $Rg_*$ means derived sections with values in towers, without inverse limit. Restriction $\rho_*$ is exact. Use the derived internal Hom and signed closed tensor-Hom structure [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model].
Let $k$ be a field with $\ell$ invertible, and let $a:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism between finite-type $k$-schemes, with a fixed compactification $X\xrightarrow j Z\xrightarrow pY$, $pj=a$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the quotient sequence sites put $F^{\mathcal Q}=Rp_*^{\mathcal Q}j_!$, with proper image derived after exact open extension, and $F_n=Rp_{*,n}j_!$ at $A_n$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. For $K\in D(R_X)$ put $V=\operatorname{const}K$ and $M=L\rho_X^*V$, with $M_n=K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$ and actual quotient transitions [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction].
For arbitrary $U,N\in D(\mathcal Q_X)$ put $D=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal Q_X}(U,N)$, $h=Rg_{X*}^{\mathcal Q}D$, $L=Lg_Y^{\mathcal Q*}h$, $b_U=Rg_{Y*}^{\mathcal Q}F^{\mathcal Q}U$, and $b_N=Rg_{Y*}^{\mathcal Q}F^{\mathcal Q}N$. Use pullback composition $La^{\mathcal Q*}L\cong Lg_X^{\mathcal Q*}h$, the sections counit $Lg_X^{\mathcal Q*}Rg_{X*}^{\mathcal Q}D\to D$, and closed evaluation to specify
$$v_{U,N}:U\otimes^L La^{\mathcal Q*}L\longrightarrow U\otimes^LD\longrightarrow N.$$
The last arrow uses the graded symmetry and the recorded evaluation, whose K-flat/K-injective model sends a sheafified homogeneous pure tensor to the corresponding Hom evaluation with that symmetry convention.
Use the canonical projection mate $\pi_f$ characterized as the adjunct of $(\varepsilon_{f,E}\otimes1)\mu_f$, for $f=p^{\mathcal Q},g_Y^{\mathcal Q},\rho_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Let
$$\Pi_{U,L}:F^{\mathcal Q}U\otimes^LL\xrightarrow{\pi_p}Rp_*^{\mathcal Q}(j_!U\otimes^LLp^{\mathcal Q*}L)\xrightarrow{Rp_*(\gamma)}F^{\mathcal Q}(U\otimes^LLa^{\mathcal Q*}L),$$
where $\gamma$ is the actual open tensor comparison of [lem-coef-support-open-tensor-model] followed by pullback composition. Let
$$q_{U,N}:b_U\otimes^L_{\mathcal A}h\xrightarrow{\pi_{g_Y}}Rg_{Y*}^{\mathcal Q}(F^{\mathcal Q}U\otimes^LL)\xrightarrow{Rg_{Y*}(F^{\mathcal Q}(v_{U,N})\Pi_{U,L})}b_N.$$
For $H,B\in D(\mathcal A)$ specify scalar balancing by the composite
$$c_{H,B}:\rho_{0*}H\otimes_R^L\rho_{0*}B\xrightarrow{\pi_{\rho_0}}\rho_{0*}(H\otimes_{\mathcal A}^LL\rho_0^*\rho_{0*}B)\xrightarrow{\rho_{0*}(1\otimes\varepsilon_{\rho_0,B})}\rho_{0*}(H\otimes_{\mathcal A}^LB).$$
These formulas give a well-defined representative-independent derived system map
$$\widetilde\beta_{U,N}=\rho_{0*}(q_{U,N}\circ\sigma_{h,b_U})\circ c_{h,b_U}:\rho_{0*}h\otimes_R^L\rho_{0*}b_U\longrightarrow\rho_{0*}b_N.$$
It is realized by the ordinary module adjunctions and their simultaneous derived functors on the ringed sequence sites. No finite-Tor condition on $L$ or invertibility of a projection mate is needed. In particular for $U=M$ the Hom comparison and compact-support comparison transport it to a map $\mathsf H_N(K)\otimes_R^LB_K\to B_N$, where $\mathsf H_N(K)$ and its Hom comparison are those of [lem-coef-hom-tower-scalar-model], $B_K=\rho_{0*}b_M$ and $B_N=\rho_{0*}b_N$.

proof.text: Apply the ringed-site derived adjunction and projection-mate theorem to $p^{\mathcal Q}$, $g_Y^{\mathcal Q}$, $g_X^{\mathcal Q}$ and $\rho_0$. Their source and target sites are small by the ringed sequence-site construction and the stated skeleton convention, and their coefficient sheaves are commutative. Thus $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ and the counits used here exist on the ordinary unbounded derived categories. For $p^{\mathcal Q},g_Y^{\mathcal Q},\rho_0$, take exactly the mate of $(\varepsilon_{f,E}\otimes1)\mu_f$; this gives the three specified projection maps, for arbitrary second tensor factor. The theorem requires neither finite Tor amplitude nor invertibility of these maps.

In the closed symmetric monoidal derived category of the quotient sequence site, set $D=R\mathcal Hom(U,N)$ and $h=Rg_{X*}^{\mathcal Q}D$. Pullback composition for $g_X^{\mathcal Q}=g_Y^{\mathcal Q}a^{\mathcal Q}$ identifies $La^{\mathcal Q*}L$ with $Lg_X^{\mathcal Q*}h$. Apply the sections counit to obtain $t:La^{\mathcal Q*}L\to D$. If $e_{U,N}:D\otimes^LU\to N$ denotes closed evaluation, then $v_{U,N}=e_{U,N}\circ\sigma_{U,D}\circ(1_U\otimes t)$. This has source $U\otimes^LLa^{\mathcal Q*}L$ and target $N$. The recorded tensor-Hom model identifies $e$ with actual Hom evaluation on K-flat/K-injective representatives; the symmetry on degrees $(r,s)$ contributes $(-1)^{rs}$. Thus the stated evaluation convention, including its sign, specifies this map.

source.place: Tags 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom); signed evaluation in the recorded tensor-Hom model.

proof.text: Apply $\pi_p$ with $E=j_!U$ and second factor $L$; its target is $Rp_*^{\mathcal Q}(j_!U\otimes^LLp^{\mathcal Q*}L)$. Apply the open tensor comparison to $U$ and $Lp^{\mathcal Q*}L$. The equality of coefficient restrictions $j^{-1}\mathcal Q_Z=\mathcal Q_X$, including the horizontal quotient maps, is part of the cited open comparison. Its target is $Rp_*^{\mathcal Q}j_!(U\otimes^LLj^{\mathcal Q*}Lp^{\mathcal Q*}L)$. Pullback composition for $pj=a$ identifies the last input with $U\otimes^LLa^{\mathcal Q*}L$. This is precisely $\Pi_{U,L}$. The cited open map is defined on the whole derived sequence site, so this construction is not an assembly of independently chosen finite-level morphisms.

proof.text: Now use $\pi_{g_Y}$ with $E=F^{\mathcal Q}U$ and second factor $h$. Since $Lg_Y^{\mathcal Q*}h=L$, it maps $b_U\otimes^L_{\mathcal A}h$ to $Rg_{Y*}^{\mathcal Q}(F^{\mathcal Q}U\otimes^LL)$. The morphism $F^{\mathcal Q}(v_{U,N})\circ\Pi_{U,L}$ maps the latter inner object to $F^{\mathcal Q}N$. Applying $Rg_{Y*}^{\mathcal Q}$ and composing gives exactly $q_{U,N}:b_U\otimes^L_{\mathcal A}h\to b_N$. All adjacent sources and targets agree; this is ordinary functoriality and composition in the derived categories.

source.place: Tag 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), with the preceding evaluation and open comparison.

proof.text: Use $\pi_{\rho_0}$ with $E=H$ and second factor $\rho_{0*}B$. Exactness of scalar restriction identifies its right derived functor with $\rho_{0*}$. Tensor the counit $L\rho_0^*\rho_{0*}B\to B$ by $H$ and apply $\rho_{0*}$; the resulting composite is the displayed $c_{H,B}$. With $H=h$ and $B=b_U$, its target is $\rho_{0*}(h\otimes^L_{\mathcal A}b_U)$. Compose with $\rho_{0*}(q_{U,N}\circ\sigma_{h,b_U})$ to reach $\rho_{0*}b_N$. This gives precisely $\widetilde\beta_{U,N}$ with the required order of factors; scalar balancing is this composite, not an identification of the two tensor products.

proof.text: The ordinary module adjunction for each ringed morphism has pullback $S\otimes_{f^{-1}R}f^{-1}(-)$ and pushforward with its structural scalar action. Its derived adjunction, the tensor comparison, and pullback composition are the canonical ones of the cited derived-mate and monoidal-comparison theorems. The closed evaluation has the natural K-flat/K-injective comparison of the recorded model, and the open comparison is already a transformation of derived sequence functors. Consequently every arrow composed above is defined after localization, with these fixed representative comparisons. Replacing representatives merely conjugates each arrow by its natural comparison isomorphisms; the intermediate inverse/isomorphism pairs cancel in the composite. This proves representative independence and realization by the ordinary module adjunctions and their derived functors simultaneously on sequence sites. No inverse-limit functor or finite-evaluation faithfulness is used.

For $U=M=L\rho_X^*(\operatorname{const}K)$, use the scalar Hom-model theorem with $W=X$ and this $N$. It gives a natural isomorphism $\eta:\mathsf H_N(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\rho_{0*}h$. The support comparison identifies $B_K=\rho_{0*}b_M$ with point sections of the strict compact-support reduction tower. Define the asserted transported map to be $\widetilde\beta_{M,N}\circ(\eta\otimes1_{B_K}):\mathsf H_N(K)\otimes_R^LB_K\to B_N$, with $B_N=\rho_{0*}b_N$. This states the transport explicitly. Both comparison theorems apply to arbitrary ambient $K$ (and the Hom theorem to arbitrary $N$), so no constructibility, normalization or finite-Tor hypothesis has been introduced.
